glossa.text: *But the souls of the just.* ((RAB.)) In the former chapter the sentence of the wicked was set forth, etc., *as far as* whence: *Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints ((Psal. CXV))*.
*Sparks.* A spark does two things, namely, it swiftly changes a reed-bed, and it avenges.

*And the Lord shall reign.* With whom his members also shall reign. Whence in Daniel: *The kingdom and the power, and the greatness of the kingdom, which is above heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High ((Dan. VII))* .

notes.text: Seas — The whole collection of waters, as well as the sea and the rivers running into it, as that great abyss of waters which is contained in the bowels of the earth.

The hill — Zion or Moriah, the place of God's sanctuary and special presence. Having asserted God's dominion over all mankind, he now proposes an important question, by whom God will be served, and his blessing enjoyed? Stand - To minister before him. Standing is the posture of ministers or servants. Who shall serve God, with God's acceptation. Holy place - In the place which he hath sanctified for his service.

He — Whose actions and conversation are holy and unblameable. Pure heart - Careful to approve itself to God, as well as to men; ordering a man's very thoughts and affections according to God's word. Vanity - Who doth not value or desire the vain things of this life, such as honours, riches, pleasures; but makes God his portion.
The blessing — Grace and glory, and all other good things.
The generation — The true progeny which God regards. Face - His grace and favour, which is often called God's face.

Lift up — He speaks here of the gates and doors of the temple, which by faith and the spirit of prophecy, he beheld as already built, whose doors he calls Everlasting, not so much because they were made of strong and durable materials, as in opposition to those of the tabernacle, which were removed from place to place. These gates he bids lift up their heads, or tops, by allusion to those gates which have a portcullis, which may be let down or taken up. And as the temple was a type of Christ, and of his church, and of heaven itself; so this place may also contain a representation, either of Christ's entrance into his church, or into the hearts of his faithful people, who are here commanded to set open their hearts and souls for his reception: or of his ascension into heaven, where the saints or angels are poetically introduced as preparing the way, and opening the heavenly gates to receive their Lord and king, returning to his royal habitation with triumph and glory. The king - The Messiah, the king of Israel, and of his church, called the King, or Lord of glory, 1 Cor. ii, 8 James ii, 1, both for that glory which is inherent in him, and that which is purchased by him for his members.
The Lord — He is no ordinary person, no other than Jehovah, who hath given so many proofs of his almightiness, who hath subdued all his enemies, and is now returned in triumph.

Lift up — The same verse is repeated again, to awaken the dulness of mankind, who are so hardly brought to a serious preparation for such solemnities; and to signify the great importance of the matter, contained under these expressions.

Of hosts — Under whose command are all the hosts of heaven and earth, angels and men, and all other creatures. David distrest, takes refuge in God, ver. 1-7. Shews the goodness of God to them that fear him, ver. 8-15. Prays for help against his enemies, and for the church, ver. 16-22. A psalm of David.

glossa.text: *A psalm of David.* ((AUG.)) On the first day of the week the world was founded, on the same day man was restored through the resurrection of Christ: ((CASS.)) whence he admonishes us to receive the conqueror with triumph. *The earth is the Lord's.* First he says that the whole world is God's, etc., *as far as* but who shall be in his mountain, save the innocent?

*And upon the rivers.* ((AUG.)) As rivers glide into the sea, so the covetous glide into the world; and these too the Church overcomes, which, its covetous desires being conquered, is made ready for immortality.
*Who shall ascend?* He determines with what virtues they are endowed in the Church.

*Who shall stand?* ((HIER.)) For many ascend who do not abide. ((ID.)) *The innocent:* toward his neighbour, in hand and in heart, and he who is innocent toward himself, etc., *as far as* they should desire his presence and his knowledge. *Who hath not taken.* ((AUG., HIER.)) That is, who has not reckoned his soul among things that do not abide, but perceiving it immortal shall desire things eternal, and therefore has not sworn deceitfully. *In vain.* ((HIER.)) That is, who has stained it with no dregs of sins after baptism.

*Lift up.* Diapsalmus. Christian religion having been declared, etc., *as far as* which were set there by the prince the devil. *And be ye lifted up.* Against the gates of death. *Ye everlasting gates:* all the grace which, at Christ's coming, was given.
*Who is?* he asks. The Prophet, to convict the perfidy of the Jews, and that by commending him the more he may invite others.

*The Lord strong* is described by his powers as though by his proper name. *Strong,* ((AUG.)) even if ye took him with swords.

*Mighty,* even if ye delivered him to Pilate.

 *Mighty in battle,* lest ye think ye have overcome him in the fight. *The powers.* ((Hier., AUG.)) The ministering powers going before Christ in the ascension cry out to the other heavenly ones, that they may open the way to the Lord as he comes: and these, astonished at the new mystery of one clothed in flesh, ask, who is he?

*Lift up.* ((CASS.)) A doubling, etc., *as far as* who gives all good things to all, or of the heavenly powers, that is, of the angels.

notes.text: And I saw — So it runs, chap. xix, 11, xx, 1, 4, 11, in a succession. All these several representations follow one another in order: so the vision reaches into eternity. A new heaven and a new earth - After the resurrection and general judgment. St. John is not now describing a flourishing state of the church, but a new and eternal state of all things. For the first heaven and the first earth - Not only the lowest part of heaven, not only the solar system, but the whole ethereal heaven, with all its host, whether of planets or fixed stars, Isai xxxiv, 4 Matt. xxiv, 29. All the former things will be done away, that all may become new, verses 4, 5, 2 Pet. iii, 10, 12. Are passed away - But in the fourth verse it is said, "are gone away." There the stronger word is used; for death, mourning, and sorrow go away all together: the former heaven and earth only pass away, giving place to the new heaven and the new earth.

And I saw the holy city — The new heaven, the new earth, and the new Jerusalem, are closely connected. This city is wholly new, belonging not to this world, not to the millennium, but to eternity. This appears from the series of the vision, the magnificence of the description, and the opposition of this city to the second death, chap. xx, 11, 12; xxi, 1, 2, 5, 8, 9; xxii, 5. Coming down - In the very act of descending.
They shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God — So shall the covenant between God and his people be executed in the most glorious manner.

And death shall be no more — This is a full proof that this whole description belongs not to time, but eternity. Neither shall sorrow, or crying, or pain, be any more: for the former things are gone away - Under the former heaven, and upon the former earth, there was death and sorrow, crying and pain; all which occasioned many tears: but now pain and sorrow are fled away, and the saints have everlasting life and joy.

And he that sat upon the throne said — Not to St. John only. From the first mention of "him that sat upon the throne," chap. iv, 2, this is the first speech which is expressly ascribed to him. And he - The angel. Saith to me Write - As follows. These sayings are faithful and true - This includes all that went before. The apostle seems again to have ceased writing, being overcome with ecstasy at the voice of him that spake.

And he — That sat upon the throne. Said to me, It is done - All that the prophets had spoken; all that was spoken, chap. iv, 1. We read this expression twice in this prophecy: first, chap. xvi, 17, at the fulfilling of the wrath of God; and here, at the making all things new. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end - The latter explains the former: the Everlasting. I will give to him that thirsteth - The Lamb saith the same, chap. xxii, 17.

glossa.text: *And I saw.* In this seventh vision he treats of the renewing of the elements and the glorification of the saints, describing the merits through which the saints are thus glorified. *A new heaven and a new earth.* The change of the air and of the earth is not doubtful, but that it comes to pass through fire. But concerning water there is doubt, for it is believed to have purgation in itself.

*As a bride adorned.* As a bridegroom sends gifts beforehand to his bride before he leads her home, so does Christ send to the Church faith and virtues and good works before he receives her into glory.

*A great voice from the throne.* When he had said that he had seen the renewing of the elements and the glorification of the saints, this was unknown, and, lest it should seem past believing, he adds the authority of the holy Fathers, who foretold this. *Behold the tabernacle.* That is, it is plain that the humanity of Christ shall be in that same glory in which it warred, and the men who imitated him and used those things well.

 *And they his people.* That is, offending in nothing, which cannot be while they are in mortal flesh.
*And death.* Truly there shall be no tears there, because there shall be no cause of tears.

*And he said.* As if he should say: Write whatsoever has been shown thee concerning this renewing. This was done for the profit of those now present, for whom I have been bidden to write these things. *Write: for these,* etc. Bidding him write, and announce to others, he subjoins an exhortation, that all may labour to belong to this renewing.

*And he said to me.* When the authority of the saints concerning this renewing has been set down, he sets down the authority of God himself. *It is done.* Lest anyone should ask: What shall come to pass after that renewing, it is said to him that nothing remains to be done.

 *Alpha and Omega.* As if he should say: This renewing I shall be able to make, because I created all things, and in me all things shall be consummated. *To him that thirsteth.* I will give, not to him that thirsteth for an hour, but to him that perseveres.

notes.text: She fell at his feet — This Martha had not done. So she makes amends for her slowness in coming.

He groaned — So he restrained his tears. So he stopped them soon after, ver. 38. He troubled himself - An expression amazingly elegant, and full of the highest propriety. For the affections of Jesus were not properly passions, but voluntary emotions, which were wholly in his own power. And this tender trouble which he now voluntarily sustained, was full of the highest order and reason.
Jesus wept — Out of sympathy with those who were in tears all around him, as well as from a deep sense of the misery sin had brought upon human nature.
Could not this person have even caused, that this man should not have died? — Yet they never dreamed that he could raise him again! What a strange mixture of faith and unbelief.

It was a cave — So Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their wives, except Rachel, were buried in the cave of Machpelah, Gen. xlix, 29-31. These caves were commonly in rocks, which abounded in that country, either hollowed by nature or hewn by art. And the entrance was shut up with a great stone, which sometimes had a monumental inscription.
Lord, by this time he stinketh — Thus did reason and faith struggle together.
Said I not — It appears by this, that Christ had said more to Martha than is before recorded.

Jesus lifted up his eyes — Not as if he applied to his Father for assistance. There is not the least show of this. He wrought the miracle with an air of absolute sovereignty, as the Lord of life and death. But it was as if he had said, I thank thee, that by the disposal of thy providence, thou hast granted my desire, in this remarkable opportunity of exerting my power, and showing forth thy praise.
He cried with a loud voice — That all who were present might hear. Lazarus, come forth - Jesus called him out of the tomb as easily as if he had been not only alive, but awake also.

And he came forth bound hand and foot with grave clothes — Which were wrapt round each hand and each foot, and his face was wrapt about with a napkin - If the Jews buried as the Egyptians did, the face was not covered with it, but it only went round the forehead, and under the chin; so that he might easily see his way.

glossa.text: *He groaned in the spirit.* Note the power: he himself groaned and troubled himself, whom another could not trouble, as he took upon himself all things of this kind because he willed it. And it signifies how greatly a man ought to be troubled when pressed by so great a mass of sin. But when the sinner, reckoning what good things of God he has received and what evils he has rendered, groans in spirit and is troubled, Christ groans in him and is troubled, because faith concerning Christ is Christ in the heart. But faith groans in a man while he rebukes himself for his sins.

*Where have you laid him?* He who though absent knew that he was dead knows also where he is buried; but speaking thus, he signifies that he as it were does not know the lost man; whence it is said: *I know you not ((Matth. VII))*. And: *Where is Adam? ((Gen. III.))*

*Jesus therefore,* etc. He shows the difficulty of the quickening of such a sinner. *Now it was a cave.* Morally: every sinner pressed by the mass of his sins and weighed down by his own law, and now stinking by his own evil habit, openly corrupts others by his bad example: the sisters are certain thoughts, because sometimes, thinking that he has done ill, he grieves.
*Lord, by this time he stinketh.* She feared that, the stone being taken away, the stench would rather be stirred up than her brother raised.

*But for the people,* etc. By these words he shows that he seeks the glory of the Father, as in his other works. For because according to his manhood he was less than the Father, he asks of him the raising of Lazarus, and therefore says that he was heard, and this for the sake of the bystanders, that they might so believe him the Son of God.

*With a loud voice.* He groaned, he wept, he cried out, because he rises with difficulty whom the mass of an evil habit presses; but nevertheless after the great voice he rises, that is, by the great grace of God he is quickened while he repents.

*And forthwith he came forth.* While the sinner despises, he lies buried; when he repents, he rises; when he confesses, he comes forth, as though going out of hiding into the open. *Loose him.* Christ by himself quickens within; to his ministers he grants the power of loosing.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God.
No torment will ever touch them.
Lift up your heads, O gates;
the King of glory comes in.
See, the home of God is among mortals.
Death will be no more, and every tear wiped away.
Come, let us worship with all the saints.
We come, and they come with us. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: At the tomb of his friend Jesus wept, and then he called with a loud voice: Lazarus, come out! Unbind him, and let him go.
God will wipe away every tear.
For the souls of the faithful are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them; they are at peace.
God will wipe away every tear.
See, God is making all things new — a new heaven, a new earth, and death itself undone.
God will wipe away every tear.
So lift up your heads, you gates; the King of glory is coming, and a great cloud of witnesses comes with him. Come, let us worship.
God will wipe away every tear. Amen.
